note: Withdrawable fact pool for the manufacturing scenario, seeded from public CPSC/NHTSA recall and defect-report patterns. Facts paraphrased; each record funds one distinct page.
sources: CPSC/NHTSA recall and defect report structure (public domain) — affected unit, defect, contributing factors, corrective action

records.description_body: Line 3 produced housings with a hairline crack defect affecting 4.2 percent of a run over a five hour window.
records.timeline_body: A cavity pressure deviation alarm fired at 06:31; the first flagged part appeared at 06:40 and production paused after a hold at 11:40.
records.contributing_body: Mold-controller firmware 2.0.5 compensates too slowly for pressure deviation under melt-temperature drift.
records.action: Upgrade to mold-controller firmware 2.1.1, or shorten the pressure-sensor calibration interval on 2.0.5.

records.description_body: Line 5 produced short-shot parts affecting 2.8 percent of a run over a three hour window.
records.timeline_body: A melt-temperature low alarm preceded the defects; the lot was placed on quality hold.
records.contributing_body: A clogged nozzle heater on firmware 2.0.6 caused inconsistent melt temperature.
records.action: Replace the nozzle heater and add melt-temperature trend alerting.

records.description_body: Assembly Line 2 produced units with a torque out-of-spec fastener defect over a four hour window.
records.timeline_body: A torque-tool calibration alert was missed; downstream inspection caught the defect and held the lot.
records.contributing_body: A drifting torque tool on controller firmware 2.0.5 applied insufficient fastener torque.
records.action: Recalibrate torque tools and enforce calibration-alert acknowledgement.

records.description_body: Line 7 produced surface-blemish parts affecting 1.1 percent of a run over a two hour window.
records.timeline_body: A mold-surface temperature warning triggered; a brief hold cleared the blemish condition.
records.contributing_body: A mold-surface temperature sensor lag on firmware 2.1.0 delayed compensation.
records.action: Update the sensor firmware to 2.1.2 and verify surface-temperature response.

records.description_body: Extrusion Line 1 produced out-of-diameter profile over a three hour window affecting 3.4 percent of output.
records.timeline_body: A puller-speed deviation preceded the defect; the lot was held for dimensional inspection.
records.contributing_body: A puller-speed control drift on firmware 2.0.6 varied the extrusion diameter.
records.action: Recalibrate puller-speed control and update to 2.1.1.

records.description_body: Assembly Line 4 produced a missing-component defect over a one hour window caught by vision inspection.
records.timeline_body: A feeder jam went undetected briefly; vision inspection flagged the missing component and held the lot.
records.contributing_body: A feeder-jam sensor blind spot on controller firmware 2.0.5 delayed detection.
records.action: Reposition the feeder-jam sensor and update to 2.1.2.

records.description_body: Line 9 produced warped parts over a five hour window affecting 5.1 percent of a run.
records.timeline_body: A cooling-time deviation alarm fired; production paused after a root-cause hold.
records.contributing_body: An insufficient cooling-time setting on firmware 2.1.0 caused part warping.
records.action: Correct the cooling-time recipe and update to 2.1.2.

records.description_body: Assembly Line 6 produced a mislabeled-unit defect over a four hour window affecting 2.0 percent of output.
records.timeline_body: A label-printer sync fault produced offset labels; downstream scanning caught the defect.
records.contributing_body: A label-printer synchronization fault on firmware 2.0.6 offset the applied labels.
records.action: Resynchronize the label printer and update to 2.1.1.
